title: Set 62

sentences.ko: 우리 이십 분째 넘기고만 있잖아. 그러니까 이제 그냥 아무거나 골라, 나는 그거 볼게. 근데 또 그런 범죄 다큐 틀면 나 옆에서 또 잠들 거고, 그럼 너는 나 때문에 껐다고 또 화내겠지.
sentences.text: We've been scrolling for twenty minutes, so at this point just pick something and I'll watch it. But if you put on another one of those crime documentaries I'm going to fall asleep on you again, and then you'll be mad at me for making you stop it.

alts.text: That's twenty minutes of scrolling. Just pick anything and I'll watch it. But if you throw on another one of those crime docs I'm gonna fall asleep on you again, and then you'll be mad at me for making you stop it.

We have been scrolling for twenty minutes, so at this point please choose something and I will watch it. However, if you put on another one of those crime documentaries, I am going to fall asleep on you again, and then you will be upset with me for making you stop it.

sentences.note: **put on** 은 영상이나 음악을 트는 것입니다. **fall asleep on you** 는 상대가 옆에 있는데 그 앞에서 잠들어 버린다는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 토요일에 제스랑 그 수업 갔었는데, 솔직히 아무렇지도 않게 넘어간 줄 알았거든. 근데 지금은 뭘 붙잡지 않으면 앉지를 못해. 제일 괴로운 건 계단이야. 오늘 아침에는 한 층 올라가는데 노인네처럼 엘리베이터를 탔어. 누가 봤든 신경도 안 쓰여.
sentences.text: I went to that class with Jess on Saturday, and I honestly thought I got away with it, but now I can't sit down without grabbing onto something. Stairs are the worst part. I took the elevator up one floor this morning like an old man, and I don't even care who saw me.

alts.text: Saturday I did that class with Jess, and I swear I thought I got away with it, but now I can't sit down without holding onto something. Stairs are the worst. I rode the elevator up one floor this morning like an old man, and I honestly don't care who saw.

I attended that class with Jess on Saturday, and I genuinely believed I had gotten away with it, but now I cannot sit down without holding on to something. The stairs are the worst part. I took the elevator up a single floor this morning like an old man, and I do not even care who saw me.

sentences.note: **got away with it** 은 치를 대가를 안 치르고 그냥 넘어갔다는 뜻입니다. **grabbing onto something** 은 뭔가를 붙잡는다는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 걔네한테는 내일 아침 일찍 일정이 있다고 할 거야. 사실이긴 해, 열한 시라서 그렇지. 피곤하다고 하면 다들 딱 한 잔만 더 하고 가라고 붙잡을 거고, 그럼 또 한 시간이잖아. 그러니까 그 얘기 나오면 너도 맞다고 거들어 줘, 알았지?
sentences.text: I'm going to tell them I've got an early thing tomorrow, which is true, it's just at eleven. Because if I say I'm tired they'll all start telling me to stay for one more, and then that's another hour. So back me up if it comes up, alright?

alts.text: Here's the plan, I'll tell them I've got an early thing tomorrow, which is true, it's just at eleven. Cause if I say I'm tired they'll all start telling me to stay for one more, and then that's another hour. So back me up if it comes up, yeah?

I am going to tell them that I have an early commitment tomorrow, which is true, it is simply at eleven. If I say that I am tired, they will all begin telling me to stay for one more, and then that becomes another hour. So please support me if it comes up.

sentences.note: **back me up** 은 내 말이 맞다고 옆에서 편들어 준다는 뜻입니다. **stay for one more** 는 한 잔 더 하고 가라는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 저녁 모임에서 먼저 일어날 구실 만들기

sentences.ko: 듣기 좋은 말 해 줄까, 솔직한 말 해 줄까? 색은 너한테 진짜 잘 어울려. 내가 애매하다고 보는 건 핏이야, 어깨가 여기까지 이렇게 나와 있잖아. 아직 반품 되면 한 치수 작은 걸로 가 봐, 그럼 완전 다른 셔츠가 돼.
sentences.text: Do you want the nice answer or the real one? Because the color's great on you, it's the fit I'm not sure about, the shoulders are sitting way out here. If you can still take it back, go down a size and it's a completely different shirt.

alts.text: Nice answer or real answer? Cause the color's great on you, it's the fit I'm iffy about, the shoulders are sitting way out here. If you can still take it back, go down a size and it's a whole different shirt.

Would you prefer the kind answer or the honest one? The color is wonderful on you. It is the fit I am unsure about, as the shoulders are sitting quite far out here. If you are still able to return it, go down a size and it will be a completely different shirt.

sentences.note: **the fit** 은 옷이 몸에 맞는 정도를 말합니다. **go down a size** 는 한 치수 작은 것으로 바꾼다는 뜻이고, **take it back** 은 산 물건을 반품한다는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 친구가 산 옷 어떠냐고 물었을 때 솔직하게 말하기

sentences.ko: 우리 집 개는 폭풍이 오는 걸 우리보다 먼저 알아. 막 왔다 갔다 하기 시작하다가 욕조 안으로 들어가려고 해. 그럼 우리가 해 줄 수 있는 게 없어. 그냥 끝날 때까지 바닥에 같이 앉아 있는 거지. 지난주에는 새벽 두 시에 담요 들고 거기 앉아 있었어. 이게 이제 당연한 일이라도 되는 것처럼.
sentences.text: Our dog knows a storm is coming before we do. He starts pacing around, and then he's trying to get in the bathtub. And there's nothing you can do about it, you just sit on the floor with him until it's over. I was in there at two in the morning last week with a blanket, like that's a normal thing now.

alts.text: That dog of ours knows a storm's coming before we do. He starts pacing around, then he's trying to climb in the bathtub. And there's nothing you can do, you just sit on the floor with him till it's over. I was in there at two in the morning last week with a blanket, like that's just normal now.

Our dog is aware that a storm is approaching before we are. He begins pacing around, and then he attempts to get into the bathtub. There is nothing you can do about it. You simply sit on the floor with him until it has passed. I was in there at two in the morning last week with a blanket, as though that were a normal thing now.

sentences.note: **pacing around** 은 불안해서 가만있지 못하고 왔다 갔다 하는 것입니다. **until it's over** 는 그 상황이 끝날 때까지라는 뜻입니다.

reviewed: 1번 casual 첫머리 "Twenty minutes of scrolling now" 가 말보다 글에 가까워 "That's twenty minutes of scrolling." 로 고쳤습니다. text 와 겹치지 않으면서 입에서 나오는 말이 됩니다.
1번 한국어 마지막 문장에 "나 때문에 … 나한테" 가 겹쳐 있어 "그럼 너는 나 때문에 껐다고 또 화내겠지" 로 다듬었습니다.
5번 formal 의 "pacing about" 은 영국식이라 text 와 같은 "pacing around" 로 맞췄고, 끝의 "as though that is a normal thing now" 를 격식체에 맞는 "as though that were a normal thing now" 로 고쳤습니다.
